basis: D6 (T5, the LP-stake class): the firm filed Golden Gate Capital under its own 'Investment Partnerships' category (2008 to 2017 listings) and described it as a private equity firm; its 2014 team page says Len Baker is responsible for SHV's investment in Golden Gate Capital, 'a private equity firm in San Francisco that Sutter Hill helped found in 2000'. The position is an interest in a fund manager and its partnerships, not venture equity in an operating company.

D6 (T5, the LP-stake class): listed 2008 to 2016 under the firm's own 'Investment Partnerships' category and described there as 'a stage independent, India-focused venture fund'. A fund interest, not an operating company.

Judged on the evidence, the row is out. Its only record is one 2008 page titled 'Indus' (shv.com/investment/indus.html), filed under the firm's own 'Investment Partnerships' category (D6), whose text describes Indus International's January 2007 combination with MDSI into Ventyx. That category's text does not identify the position: the same 2008 category pairs 'Biovest', which the 1999 table lists as 'Biovest Partners, medical investment partnership, Distributed', with the unrelated Biovest International's company description. Read either way, no venture position exists: as a partnership interest (an investment firm such as Indus Capital Partners, founded 2000, fits the category) it is the LP-stake class (T5); as Indus International it was a listed company from its 1997 formation until the 2006 to 2007 buyout that merged it into Ventyx, so any SHV purchase was a public-market or buyout position (T3), and no SEC filing in the 2001 to 2024 full-text sweep ties SHV to it. Worth Erik's look beside D6.

The base carries this company twice: this row and 'mattersight' (the 2013 to 2017 listing).
